value: ethephon (an ethylene-releasing hormone treatment) did not improve seed germination in Ratibida, which stayed near 10 to 20 percent, while it raised germination to about 30 to 85 percent in the other Asteraceae sources tested
method: seeds of eight native South Dakota Asteraceae given a two-week ethephon treatment under continuous light at 5 C
conditions: seed lots from South Dakota; species within Ratibida not named on the abstract page; tetrazolium tests tied the variation to seed viability

source.title: Native Plants of the Northern Great Plains: Ethylene Induction of Asteraceae Seed Germination
source.journal: Proceedings of the South Dakota Academy of Science 79: 175

where: repository abstract page opened through WebFetch
quote: Germination was significantly increased for all seed sources (with final germination ranging from ~30 to 85%) except for those of Liatris and Ratibida, which showed no improvement.
note: Abstract only. Genus-level value, grade g: the page does not name the Ratibida species. Hormone treatment of seeds counted under sense_chemical (desk-screen 10(d,e)). The WebFetch tool returned the sentence in two pieces ('Germination was significantly increased for all seed sources (with final germination ranging from ~30 to 85%)' and 'except for those of Liatris and Ratibida, which showed no improvement.'), which are joined here; check the wording against the page. The treatment bundles ethephon with two weeks of continuous light, so no separate light effect is read.
